title: A Glance from Heaven, with Sweet Effect
description: A Glance from Heaven, with Sweet Effect in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 526 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Lightning in the Night”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A glance from heaven, with sweet ef-fect, So-me-times my pen-sive spirit cheers: But ere I can my thoughts col-lect, As sud-den-ly it dis-ap-pears.

lines: A glance from heaven, with sweet effect,
But ere I can my thoughts collect,
So lightning in the gloom of night
Which, soon as seen, are snatched away.
The lightning's flash did not create
But only showed the real state
Of what the darkness had concealed.
Just so, we by a glimpse discern
The glorious things within the veil;
That, when in darkness, we may learn
To live by faith, till light prevail.

licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
